3. The case as has been described in the plaint, in short, is that the suit lands appertaining to S.A Khatian No.142 originally belonged to one, Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh in equal share and the S.A. record was accordingly prepared and published in their names. While enjoying title and possession over the said property, they exchanged the same with those of the Indian property belonged to one Layebuddin Sarkar and accordingly, a deed of exchange was registered in between the parties on 27.01.1964. While Layebuddin Sarkar was enjoying title and possession over the properties, he sold out the same to one Habibur Rahman, predecessor of the plaintiffs at a consideration of taka 10,000.00 and executed a deed of sale on 03.04.1967, but due to time constrained, the same could not be registered on that very date, but it was agreed that the said deed would be presented for registration on the following day, but it could not be registered on the following day as Layebuddin Sarkar had to go to India and eventually, for his not coming back, the said deed remained unregistered. 

 17. Having considered the entire facts and circumstances, it appears that the present respondents, Abul Kashem and others, have been able to prove their claim by sufficient evidence that they have got their predecessor's exchanges deed duly validated by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi, on the basis of which they have been able to release the suit properties from list of vested and non-resident property and also have been able to mutate their names in the suit khatian.
